issues.legal_issue: An unequivocal statement in a High Court judgment that a finding was not challenged will not be treated as erroneous when the subsequent leave application and special leave petition do not dispute that statement.
material_facts: The High Court stated unequivocally that the appellants’ counsel had not challenged specified findings in the appeal.
The same counsel argued the appeal and filed the application seeking leave to appeal, which did not say that the High Court’s statement was incorrect.
The special leave petition also did not allege that the High Court’s statement was factually incorrect.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to accept the appellants’ contention that the High Court had incorrectly recorded that the findings were not challenged.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the unequivocal account in the High Court judgment and the silence of both the leave application and the special leave petition when assessing the later allegation that the account was wrong. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for this ruling.

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter came before the Supreme Court as an appeal from a High Court judgment.
predicates.high_court_unequivocally_recorded_no_cha: The High Court stated unequivocally that counsel had not challenged a finding in the appeal.
predicates.leave_application_silent_on_record_error: The application seeking leave to appeal did not allege that the High Court’s account of what was challenged was inaccurate.
predicates.special_leave_petition_silent_on_record_: The special leave petition did not allege that the High Court’s account of what was challenged was inaccurate.

issues.definition: When an appeal before the Supreme Court concerns an unequivocal High Court record that a finding was not challenged, and neither the leave application nor the special leave petition disputes that record, the later challenge to the record is not accepted.

issues.legal_issue: A plea that was not raised in the trial court or the High Court may be refused when raised for the first time in the Supreme Court, having regard to the circumstances and consequences of allowing it.
material_facts: The appellants argued for the first time in the Supreme Court that the deceased’s ownership was limited to a share of the estate and that the claimant could obtain only joint possession to that extent.
The plea had not been raised in either the trial court or the High Court.
Allowing the plea would require further consideration of the ownership issues and could require a remand to the High Court.
The litigation had continued for many years, and the principal contestants had died.
The appellants based their claim on a will made in their favour, and they had no relationship with the original family whose property was in dispute.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court refused to allow the appellants to raise the new plea for the first time in that appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Whether to permit a new plea for the first time on appeal is determined in light of the circumstances. The Court considered that the plea had not been raised below, that allowing it could prolong the litigation through further proceedings, the long history of the dispute, and the position of the new claimants. The co-sharer authorities cited by the appellants were not relied on to decide the procedural issue; no statutory provision or earlier case was relied on for the refusal.

rule.if: supreme_court_appeal and new_plea_not_raised_below and plea_would_require_further_proceedings and prolonged_litigation and new_claimants_unconnected_to_original_family and principal_contestants_deceased

predicates.supreme_court_appeal: The matter was an appeal before the Supreme Court.
predicates.new_plea_not_raised_below: The party raising the plea had not raised it in the trial court or the High Court.
predicates.plea_would_require_further_proceedings: Allowing the plea would require further consideration of the dispute and could require a remand.
predicates.prolonged_litigation: The dispute had already been litigated for many years.
predicates.new_claimants_unconnected_to_original_fa: The persons advancing the claim relied on a will in their favour and had no relationship with the original family whose property was disputed.
predicates.principal_contestants_deceased: The principal contestants in the dispute had died.

issues.definition: When a party in a Supreme Court appeal raises a new plea that was not raised below, and allowing it would require further proceedings in prolonged litigation involving new claimants unconnected to the original family after the principal contestants have died, the plea is not permitted.
